h1: The 7 Best Portable Monitors with Pass-Through Charging, Ranked & Reviewed
metaDescription: Ranked and reviewed by Primea: 7 portable monitors with pass-through charging, scored on wattage delivered to the laptop, panel brightness and port layout.
summary: The Plugable 15.6 inch USB-C monitor is the best pass-through portable screen because it publishes the math: 100W in, 85W out to the laptop. The ASUS ZenScreen MQ16FC is the OLED choice with bidirectional charging. The VisionOwl gives a bright 144Hz panel for less, and the cocopar 15.6 inch FHD is the proven budget route. The 4K screens look sharp but leave less power for your laptop.
intro: Pass-through charging sounds like a free feature: plug a charger into the monitor and it also feeds your laptop. The catch is that the monitor takes its own share first. A bright 4K panel can draw enough that the laptop receives far less than the charger's rating, and a thin ultrabook might sit at the same battery level while it works. The wattage the listing prints is the charger, not what reaches your laptop.

We ranked seven portable monitors by how honestly they deliver power, then by panel quality and port layout. Models that publish a wattage figure and the host share ranked highest, and those that only say pass-through scored lower. Brightness, resolution and refresh rate follow, since they affect how much current the screen eats.

products.name: Plugable 15.6" USB-C Portable Monitor with 100W Pass-Through Charging
products.verdict: The only monitor here that tells you the real wattage that reaches your laptop.
products.description:
Plugable's 15.6 inch FHD portable screen takes up to 100W of power delivery and passes 85W to the host, with two 10Gbps USB-C hub ports. It ships with a certified 1m USB-C cable but needs a 100W charger, sold separately, for the full figure.

That 85W number is the whole reason it ranks first. Every other monitor here says pass-through without telling you what the laptop actually gets, and 15W is what the screen keeps for itself. For a laptop that draws 65W under load, the Plugable keeps the battery full while you work. The hub ports are a bonus no cocopar or VisionOwl lists.

Buy it if you move between desks and want a single cable to power everything. The caveat is the missing charger and the premium price tier.
products.idealFor: Laptop users who want one cable for video and power.
products.skipIf: You want 4K or a high refresh rate on a tight budget.

products.name: ASUS ZenScreen MQ16FC 15.6 Inch 16:10 USB-C OLED Portable Monitor
products.verdict: OLED color and bidirectional pass-through, covered by a burn-in warranty.
products.description:
The MQ16FC is a 15.6 inch 16:10 OLED with 95% DCI-P3 coverage and a 1ms response time, offering bidirectional pass-through charging and auto-rotate through DisplayWidget software. ASUS gives it a 3-year warranty that covers burn-in.

OLED is the headline: black pixels switch off, so contrast is far beyond any LCD in this list. The burn-in coverage answers the standard worry about OLED. It ranks second because it lacks the Plugable's published wattage math, and the listing is new with little owner feedback. Against the VisionOwl, it has the better panel but the weaker evidence.

Buy it if image quality matters and you want ASUS backing. The caveat is the limited track record of a brand-new listing, so check what wattage your laptop needs.
products.idealFor: Creators and travelers who want OLED image quality on the go.
products.skipIf: You need documented charging wattage or a long review history.

products.name: VisionOwl Portable Monitor 16 Inch 2.5K QHD 144Hz, 470 Nits
products.verdict: A sharp 2.5K 144Hz panel at 470 nits with USB-C pass-through and full-size HDMI.
products.description:
The VisionOwl is a 16 inch 2.5K QHD screen at 144Hz and 470 nits, with USB-C pass-through, a full-size HDMI port, dual USB-C and dual VESA holes.

It sits third because the price tier is $100 to $200 and the panel is the best LCD here, but the listing does not state the pass-through wattage. That omission matters: a 144Hz, 470 nit screen is a heavier load on a charger than an FHD panel. Against the Plugable, it offers a better display and a lower price but no published power figure. The cocopar 15.6 inch is lower resolution.

Buy it if you want a bright, fast screen and your laptop charges from a 65W or larger charger. The caveat is simply that you cannot see how much reaches the host.
products.idealFor: Users who want a sharp, fast screen with USB-C convenience.
products.skipIf: You need to know exactly what wattage reaches the laptop.

products.name: cocopar Portable Monitor 15.6 Inch 1080P FHD 60Hz 85% sRGB
products.verdict: A 1080P screen with confirmed reverse charging, at the lowest cost here.
products.description:
The cocopar is a 15.6 inch 1080P panel at 60Hz covering 85% sRGB, with pass-through reverse charging, full-size HDMI, dual USB-C and two VESA holes.

Its value is that pass-through charging is confirmed and the screen is low-power, so more of the charger's wattage can reach the laptop than it can on the 4K cocopar. It has the largest review base of the budget group, which is a point in its favor. It ranks fourth because 85% sRGB is limited color, and a 60Hz refresh feels slow against the VisionOwl's 144Hz.

Buy it if you want a plain second screen with reliable charging for little money. The caveat is its basic panel, which is fine for documents but weak for creative color work.
products.idealFor: Office users who want a simple second screen that also charges.
products.skipIf: You want rich color or smooth motion.

products.name: cocopar Portable Monitor 18.5 Inch 2K QHD 120Hz 120% sRGB
products.verdict: An 18.5 inch QHD 120Hz screen with USB-C charging and a kickstand.
products.description:
This cocopar is an 18.5 inch 2K QHD screen at 120Hz with 120% sRGB, general USB-C pass-through, full-size HDMI, dual USB-C and a 75x75mm VESA pattern plus kickstand.

The bigger screen is the draw, and also the problem: more area and a higher refresh rate use more power, so less is left for the laptop. It ranks fifth in a pass-through ranking because the charging is general and unquantified. Against the 15.6 inch cocopar, it gives more room for side-by-side windows and a faster panel.

Buy it if you want near-desktop space that still travels. The caveat is the $200 to $500 price tier and the weight of an 18.5 inch screen in a bag.
products.idealFor: Remote workers who want a large travel screen with USB-C charging.
products.skipIf: You carry the monitor daily or need documented charging.

products.name: cocopar Portable Monitor 15.6 Inch 4K UHD 60Hz 145% sRGB
products.verdict: A 1.54 lb metal 4K screen where resolution costs charging headroom.
products.description:
This cocopar is a 15.6 inch 4K panel at 60Hz with 145% sRGB and a matte screen, in a 1.54 lb metal chassis. It includes USB-C pass-through, a built-in kickstand and a VESA mount.

A 4K panel pushes more pixels and uses more power, which means less of your charger reaches the laptop. That tradeoff is why it ranks sixth for this guide. It is a good screen, light and sharp, but it is a poorer charging partner than the FHD cocopar. The metal chassis does feel sturdier than the plastic-backed budget models.

Buy it if you edit images and carry a laptop with its own good battery. The caveat is that a thin ultrabook may still discharge slowly while the 4K screen is connected.
products.idealFor: Photo editors who value sharpness and low weight.
products.skipIf: Your laptop needs full power to keep up with charging.

products.name: EVICIV Portable Monitor 4K 1200 Nits 16", 3840x2400 UHD, 145% sRGB
products.verdict: A 1200 nit 4K screen built for brightness, not for charging a laptop.
products.description:
The EVICIV is a 16 inch 4K panel at 3840x2400, 1200 nits and 145% sRGB, with a matte anti-glare screen, an aluminum body and VESA 75x75mm mounting. It has general USB-C pass-through.

The 1200 nit backlight is useful outdoors, and it is also the biggest power draw on this list. A screen that bright eats the wattage a charger supplies, leaving little for the laptop. That is why it ranks last in a charging ranking despite a beautiful panel. Against the Plugable, it is the opposite philosophy: show off the display and leave the charging as a bonus.

Buy it if you work in bright light and use it with a laptop that has strong battery life. The caveat is that charging the laptop through it is not reliable.
products.idealFor: Outdoor and bright-room users who rarely rely on pass-through.
products.skipIf: You need the monitor to keep your laptop charged.

methodology.description: Monitors that publish the wattage reaching the host ranked above those that say only pass-through.

methodology.title: Power headroom

whatMatters.detail: Pass-through means a charger feeds the monitor and the monitor feeds the laptop, but the monitor keeps some power. The number that matters is wattage delivered to the laptop, not the charger rating. Look for a listing that says so, as with the Plugable's 85W, and compare it to your laptop's charger.

Many monitors do not include a charger, and the pass-through only works with a high enough one. The Plugable needs a 100W unit sold separately. Check what charger you own, and buy one that matches the monitor's input rating before you travel.

Brightness and resolution drive consumption. A 1200 nit 4K screen uses far more power than a 250 nit FHD one, leaving less for the laptop. If charging matters, favor lower-power panels such as the FHD cocopar or accept the drain with brighter screens.

Your laptop's USB-C port must support video output (DisplayPort Alt Mode) for a single-cable setup to work. Older ports may charge but not show a picture. Check your laptop's spec sheet, and keep the monitor's HDMI port as a backup.

Some monitors can also send power from a laptop or phone to the screen, so a single laptop cable runs the display. ASUS lists bidirectional pass-through on the MQ16FC. Verify the direction the listing means, since a one-way port will not run from your laptop.

cards.label: FHD
cards.text: Lower resolution means lower power draw, so more charger wattage reaches the laptop. It suits documents and email. Picks: Plugable, cocopar 15.6 inch FHD.

cards.label: 4K
cards.text: Sharper text and photos but a heavier power draw that cuts into charging headroom. Picks: cocopar 4K, EVICIV.

howToChoose.note: If charging reliability matters, take FHD or QHD. Take 4K only for editing and display quality.

cards.label: Look for
cards.text: A published pass-through wattage, a charger included or easy to buy, and hub ports if you use a keyboard or dock. Plan for a single USB-C cable to the laptop.

cards.label: In this ranking
cards.text: The Plugable passes 85W to the host and adds two 10Gbps USB-C hub ports. The cocopar 15.6 inch FHD is the cheaper low-power route.

cards.label: Spend more if
cards.text: Charging reliability or OLED image quality matters. The Plugable and ASUS ZenScreen justify the premium for that.

cards.label: Save if
cards.text: You use a laptop with strong battery life. The cocopar FHD and VisionOwl give plenty for much less.

faq.q: Will pass-through charging power my laptop fully?
faq.a: Not always. The monitor keeps part of the power, so a 100W charger on the Plugable delivers 85W to the host. Check your laptop's charger rating and compare it with the host figure before relying on the monitor.

faq.q: What is the most common mistake with pass-through monitors?
faq.a: Plugging in a low-power phone charger. Monitors like the Plugable need a 100W unit for the full figure, and the EVICIV's 1200 nit panel needs more still. Use a charger that matches the monitor's rating.

faq.q: Is the Plugable worth it over the cocopar?
faq.a: If charging matters, yes. The Plugable publishes 85W to the host and adds 10Gbps hub ports. The cocopar FHD costs less and confirms pass-through but does not state the wattage.

faq.q: How do I set up a single-cable workflow?
faq.a: Connect the charger to the monitor's power USB-C port, then run a USB-C cable from the monitor to your laptop. The Plugable includes a certified 1m cable. Your laptop port must support video output.

faq.q: Does the OLED ASUS risk burn-in?
faq.a: OLED can burn in with static images. ASUS covers it with a 3-year warranty that includes burn-in, and auto-rotate software adds convenience. Use dark mode and a moving wallpaper to reduce the risk.

faq.q: Can I charge a phone through these monitors?
faq.a: Often yes, through a spare USB-C port. The Plugable has two 10Gbps hub ports, and the VisionOwl and cocopar models have dual USB-C. Expect slow charging, since the screen draws first.

finalTake: The Plugable 15.6 inch USB-C monitor is the pass-through portable screen to buy because it is honest about power: 100W in and 85W to the laptop. The ASUS ZenScreen MQ16FC is the OLED upgrade with a burn-in warranty, and the VisionOwl gives the best LCD for the money. The 4K screens are lovely, but they take charging headroom with them.
